newsitem.title: UK: Prism picked for rail contract, sees rights.
newsitem.headline: Prism picked for rail contract, sees rights.

text.p: Britain's Prism Rail Plc said on Thursday it had been selected by the government's Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) as preferred bidder for the West Anglian Great Northern Railway Ltd train operating company.

In a statement AIM-listed Prism said that it intended to fund the privatisation-linked franchise partly out of the proceeds of a rights issue, "the terms of which will be finalised following the signing of the new franchise agreement".
It expected that new shares to be issued in such a rights issue would be at a price of 330 pence per share.
Prism, which was specifically formed to pursue the opportunities in rail privatisation, was awarded its first franchise, for LTS Rail, in May this year.
It has since won two more, the neigbouring South Wales & West and Cardiff Railway contracts, which it took over in September.
West Anglia/Great Northern (WAGN) has various groups of services in its franchise area which serve a mixture of commuter and regional markets to the immediate north east of London.
It operates Great Northern routes from London Kings Cross station, West Anglia routes from Liverpool Street and suburban services from Moorgate.
